newsitem.title: GERMANY: ROWING-GERMANY DOMINATE FIRST DAY OF WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: ROWING-GERMANY DOMINATE FIRST DAY OF WORLD CUP.

text.p: Germany dominated the first day of racing in the new rowing world cup competition at the Olympic regatta course in Munich on Friday.

Fourteen boats from the host nation qualified for the semifinals after the heats and repechages. Most striking were the women's quadruple sculls with German wins in both heats, while the two German men's quads also qualified directly.

Double quadruple sculls Olympic champion Andre Willms won his single sculls heat, as did the new-look German eight. The two German men's double sculls also qualified directly. The strong head wind made racing conditions slow and affected times.
This regatta provides the first opportunity for many nations to race new crew combinations put together in the traditional reshaping of squads in the post-Olympic year.

Four-times Olympic gold medallist Steven Redgrave and former pairs partner Matthew Pinsent continued their winning form in Britain's new coxless four, joined by Tim Foster and James Cracknell. They won their heat comfortably.

Redgrave, who had his appendix out last month, said: "We're pretty pleased with that. As a crew we're very inexperienced and the build-up hasn't been ideal. We're behind schedule a bit but we're coming back. We know there's a lot more to come."
Briton Greg Searle, Olympic coxed pair champion in 1992 and bronze medallist in the coxless four in Atlanta, has moved to the single sculls this season and won his heat impressively.
The world cup regatta semifinals are on Saturday, with the finals on Sunday.
